key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation and ANN model can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE and identify process windows that minimize defects while stabilizing heat and force.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a practical route to optimize polymer FSW settings—especially rotational speed, traverse speed, and bottom preheating—to improve joint integrity and reduce wormhole formation.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE friction stir welding
Two multilayer perceptron ANN models trained on experimental temperature and axial-force histories
Process-map generation across rotational speed, welding speed, and preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R² values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched experiments in predicting thermal response, axial force, and void formation.
watch_item: The optimized conditions are validated for the tested HDPE and parameter range, so transfer to other polymers, tool geometries, or larger-scale production may require re-calibration.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
